title: You Died Behind the Wall — Quantum Collapse as Netcode

shots.narration: You made it behind the wall. You saw yourself make it. Then you died anyway. What if physics has the same bug — or the same feature?

shots.sub: Experiment 001 · quantum measurement vs. FPS netcode

shots.narration: The shooter sees you ~150 ms in the past and fires at that ghost. The server receives the shot late, REWINDS the world to the shooter's snapshot, tests the hit, and makes it official — 223 ms after you reached cover.
With a half-second exposure and a 100 ms shooter, about half of all deaths happen 'behind cover' from the victim's view. It's the design.

shots.sub: a photon's pattern seems to depend on a choice made after it landed
shots.narration: Physics has a 'decided later' experiment too.
Screen hits land with no pattern. Later, their entangled twins are measured — and sorting the old hits by those later results reveals interference.
But the raw screen never changes. The pattern lives only in the JOIN of two logs — and our sim produces it strictly in time order, with no rewind. Nature needs a joint record, not a rollback.
Entangled correlations bend in a way pre-loaded answers can't match — Bell's theorem, confirmed by loophole-free tests (Nobel 2022).

Six engine architectures play the Bell game. Client-side prediction maxes at 2. A central server, a pre-written script, and keep-every-branch all hit 2.83 — collapse, superdeterminism, Many-Worlds. The same server could score 4. Nature stops at 2.83. Why?
Hosting cost: keep every branch and memory doubles per observation — 4 million amplitudes after 14. Collapse stays at 256.
From inside, the lab notebooks are statistically identical. Collapse looks like garbage collection of branches nothing can reach. (Counterpoint: that assumes a host with a budget.)

shots.sub: ✓ one canonical record · ✓ server-like correlations · ✗ branches interfere · ✗ nature never shows a contradiction · ? why 2√2 · ? why squared
shots.narration: No conclusions. Just observations. Code and sources are in the repo.
